name: Plaza Principal (Town Center)
description: The cobbled main plaza and surrounding blocks hold most of the town's shops, comedores, the bakery, and budget guesthouses. Everything is within a five to ten minute walk, and it is the natural base for anyone without a vehicle who wants easy access to minibuses, markets, and simple meals. Wifi here is as good as it gets in Coroico, which is to say inconsistent.
bestFor: short stays, budget travelers, easy transport access

name: Hillside Hotel Belt (Esmeralda / Sol y Luna area)
description: A scatter of hotels and eco-lodges on the slopes above the plaza, including Hotel Esmeralda and Sol y Luna Eco Lodge, offers sweeping Yungas valley views, pools, and quieter grounds than the center. It requires a short taxi or a steep uphill walk from the plaza, and is the best choice for anyone prioritizing scenery and a slightly more comfortable stay over walkability.
bestFor: longer stays, remote work with a view, couples
cons: 10-20 minute walk or taxi to the plaza

name: Cascadas Road (Vagantes waterfall route)
description: The dirt road and trail heading out toward the Cascadas de Vagantes waterfalls winds through coffee farms and cloud forest just outside town. A few rustic guesthouses and farm stays sit along this route, appealing to anyone who wants to wake up surrounded by forest and be first on the trail before day-trippers arrive from La Paz.
cons: rough road, especially in wet season

name: Tocaña
tagline: Afro-Bolivian village in the Yungas hills
description: A short drive from Coroico, Tocaña is a small Afro-Bolivian community known for its coffee cultivation and cultural tourism, including saya music traditions. It makes for a worthwhile day trip or a quiet overnight stay for travelers interested in the region's Afro-Bolivian heritage rather than a nomad base, since services are minimal and independent of Coroico's own infrastructure.
bestFor: cultural day trips, coffee farm visits
cons: needs a car or arranged transport from Coroico
